headline: Every finite collinear-heavy fragmentation has exact branch constant C(a)=6 E exp[-6(sum a_i U_i)^2] <= 3sqrt(2), and the supremum over this whole architecture is exactly 3sqrt(2), approached by equal weights.

mathematical_premises.scope: Exact global-output reduction of arbitrary independent cap-one collinear heavy laws to centered unit intervals; branch constant C(a)=6 E exp[-6(sum a_i U_i)^2].

mathematical_premises.source: König-Koldobsky, Advances in Mathematics 346 (2019), Proposition 7, DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2019.02.017
mathematical_premises.scope: For p>=9/4, integral_R |sin u/u|^p du <= sqrt(6 pi/p).
Exact-rank-three (+,+,-) one-sheet s>=0 ruled bound; source explicitly leaves two-sheet s<0 side open in general.

partner_result_applied.application: For a fixed independent diffuse minority-sign mode -delta, the equal-weight endpoint is exactly 3sqrt(2)/sqrt(1+delta), while convolution and the new theorem give every finite collinear member <=3sqrt(2).

unresolved_implication: Control genuinely non-collinear/coupled heavy rows (especially the source-identified two-sheet/convex side and higher-rank coupled tails) or construct a valid target counterexample; the present theorem does not imply the full universal constant is 3sqrt(2).
next_step: Attack a two- or three-heavy non-collinear original-coordinate frame using an integrated half-Riesz/ruled kernel, preserving product provenance and avoiding pointwise radial-Laplace domination.
